runtime.execution: Rust main drives a multithreaded Tokio runtime; native unified provider/action loop and owned blocking/event-drain work. A configured codex provider selects a distinct Codex App Server adapter. Python/JavaScript snippets are fresh external interpreter processes, not the core.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns context, session stores, execution/PTY handles, child tasks and managed background subprocess desired state; consumes model providers and MCP/web services. These owned processes are not a shared fabric governor.

summary: A broad Rust agent with planning, tracked execution, parent/child control, dynamic skill/catalog changes, multi-strategy compaction and canonical retained event stores. Strong persistence/error oracles coexist with limited audit retention and a source-inferred repeated-child-follow-up race.

inspection.scope: Native entry/runtime selection through request snapshots/concrete OpenAI HTTP, tool admission/dispatch/results/continuation; public versus removed tools, execution sessions, memory/cron, children/background restoration, compaction/artifacts, canonical persistence/retention/query, skills/config activation, update restart, verifier API and relevant tests.
inspection.limits: Source read only, reference not executed. Optional Codex App Server internals, provider variants, full web implementations, OS sandbox/process-tree semantics and complete checkpoint navigation are outside this trace. No paid/network/refit/concurrent-child experiments were run. Canonical events are retained rather than unlimited originals, and the inferred Waiting/restart overlap requires an independent controlled oracle.

actions.name: exec_command
actions.input: cmd; optional workdir, tty, background, yielding/output limits and sandbox request
actions.output: output, exit code or reusable session_id; spool metadata when output is bounded
actions.lifecycle: owned pipe/PTY process; explicit waits can return in-progress; background sessions retained separately
actions.authority: model admitted by command, sandbox and session policy; confirmation skipping is separate

actions.name: write_stdin
actions.input: session_id; chars or action=write/poll/wait; optional yield/wait deadline
actions.output: new bounded output and ongoing/completed session state
actions.lifecycle: wait deadline preserves the handle; actual dispatcher has no inspect/terminate/close actions
actions.authority: model continuation of an admitted owned session

actions.name: code_search
actions.input: literal query or alternatives, path/type/result filters and result limit
actions.output: workspace definition/usage/text/path matches
actions.lifecycle: awaited native search; eligible readonly group overlap
actions.authority: model; native Allow default plus public admission

actions.name: apply_patch
actions.input: patch input, optionally encoded input normalized by handler
actions.output: structured patch result/errors and affected paths
actions.lifecycle: awaited mutation, hooks/policy validation and code-change tracking
actions.authority: model; default Prompt, active policy can permit

actions.name: memory
actions.input: command=view/create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename with virtual /memories paths and text
actions.output: note listing/content or mutation acknowledgement/error
actions.lifecycle: persistent files survive sessions; generated/other paths restricted
actions.authority: model; feature/config dependent, selected writable note locations

actions.name: cron
actions.input: action=create/list/delete; prompt and exactly one cron/delay_minutes/run_at; delete ID
actions.output: scheduled task summaries/IDs, list or deletion record
actions.lifecycle: prompts scheduled inside current runtime; end at process exit
actions.authority: model; session tool budget and schedule validation

actions.name: agent: spawn / spawn_subprocess
actions.input: agent type, message/items, optional model/effort, fork_context/background/max_turns
actions.output: child ID/status or managed subprocess record and transcript/exec identities
actions.lifecycle: owned child task or separate VTCode process; background desired records can respawn
actions.authority: model with controller, depth/concurrency/config and operator delegation signals

actions.name: agent: send_input / resume / wait / close
actions.input: child ID(s), follow-up message/items, interrupt flag, wait timeout
actions.output: child status/summary/error; wait returns terminal target or timeout
actions.lifecycle: default follow-up queued; interrupt aborts current task and replaces queued prompts; close cascades; source-inferred repeated-follow-up overlap concern
actions.authority: model through active parent controller; not a peer broadcast room

actions.name: mcp
actions.input: action=search_tools/get_tool_details/list_servers/connect/disconnect; query/name
actions.output: discovery results, schemas/server state or lifecycle errors
actions.lifecycle: external server discovery and connection management; invocation tools registered separately
actions.authority: model; Allow base metadata, connection action/config authority is separate

actions.name: search_tools
actions.input: natural-language capability query and optional limit
actions.output: ranked session tools and expanded_for_next_segment
actions.lifecycle: deferred tools become available on the next request segment
actions.authority: model catalog discovery

actions.name: web_fetch / web_search
actions.input: URL or query and registered tool-specific parameters
actions.output: configured web content or search result payloads
actions.lifecycle: awaited external network operations; registered handlers, detailed network implementations outside this trace
actions.authority: model when catalog/config/provider exposure permits; fetch is prompted by default

actions.name: start_planning / task_tracker
actions.input: planning prompt/plan parameters; tracker create/update/list/add task metadata
actions.output: plan and persisted hierarchical task/checklist state
actions.lifecycle: compiled planning workflow and optional build-agent handoff; not an arbitrary workflow language
actions.authority: model, planning mode/action masks and policy

actions.name: list_skills / load_skill / load_skill_resource / activated skill names
actions.input: skill discovery query/type, selected name or active resource path; activated tool schema
actions.output: skill metadata, instructions/resource content and refreshed tools
actions.lifecycle: activation rereads an inactive skill then refreshes tools; an already-active skill returns cached content; fork skills can delegate
actions.authority: model; traditional activation policy, native/plugin/system utilities have distinct contracts

actions.name: ToolRegistry::execute_tool / execute_public_tool_ref
actions.input: tool name and JSON args, or prepared admission record
actions.output: JSON value or structured error
actions.lifecycle: awaited registry dispatch; internal and public assemblies have different accessible names
actions.authority: host programmer; removed model names remain internal compatibility machinery

actions.name: internal command_session code / CodeExecutor::execute
actions.input: Python/JavaScript program with generated MCP/builtin SDK
actions.output: stdout/stderr, exit code and parsed JSON result
actions.lifecycle: fresh interpreter/process per snippet, temporary files and shared workspace IPC; no resident globals
actions.authority: host/internal code action, subject to interpreter policy; not current public model action

actions.name: SubagentController::verify_proposed_change
actions.input: diff description and affected file paths
actions.output: approved boolean, issues and reviewer reasoning
actions.lifecycle: isolated bounded child review, sixty-second wait; no verifier rejects; keyword fallback if decision absent
actions.authority: host caller; not a registered agent action and not default reconciliation path

actions.name: session-store list / inspect / facts / pack / migrate / gc
actions.input: session/limits, audit pack output or verification path, retention/migration options
actions.output: retained store metadata/facts, hash comparison and reported missing/modified/new files
actions.lifecycle: inspect retained local material; GC/migrate mutate operator-owned stores
actions.authority: operator command; packing verifies current contents, not completeness of observations

actions.name: /feedback
actions.input: no arguments
actions.output: opens GitHub issue chooser URL or prints opening error/URL
actions.lifecycle: browser action, no tracked complaint or captured run state
actions.authority: operator via external URL approval/guard

actions.name: queued update relaunch
actions.input: relaunch preference captured after update
actions.output: replacement executable or manual restart diagnostic
actions.lifecycle: post-dispatch exec/spawn retains argv/cwd, without outpost/provider/program state transfer
actions.authority: operator update path

actions.name: defuddle_fetch
actions.input: remote http(s) URL and optional markdown byte limit
actions.output: bounded extracted markdown or error
actions.lifecycle: registered native network operation; hidden from ordinary model catalog
actions.authority: host/internal tool invocation rather than advertised model tool

filesystem.detail: Public model paths are native code_search/apply_patch and shell filesystem operations; many older read_file/list_files/edit_file registrations are expressly removed from public routes. Memory notes add a separate bounded file surface.

processes.detail: Owned pipe/PTY execution sessions have output spooling, yielding and background retention; wait/poll/input continue handles. Full close and foreground-only cancellation differ; strong test observes actual reaped PTY exit.

code_actions.detail: Internal code action builds Python/JavaScript SDK programs that can call MCP and curated builtins through IPC, but that legacy public name is removed. Model can still invoke external interpreters through exec_command; no claim of current dedicated code tool.

persistent_kernel.detail: Harness kernel is compiled catalog/mode filtering. Inspected code executor creates and deletes a fresh program/process, so neither supplies a resident namespace; externally hosted kernels could be composed through tools.

standing_database.detail: Persistent native memory files and session-store query_facts provide standing local notes/facts. Neither inspected model surface is a general shared standing database with arbitrary queries; external DB use remains composition.

workflow_programming.detail: Planning/task tools, session cron, executable lifecycle hooks, dynamic traditional skill tools and child fork execution are composable workflow pieces. The compiled loop/catalog filter is not an operator/model-defined turn/workflow program.

multi_model.detail: Child spawn accepts model/effort overrides and tests observe an effective override; parent settings can switch the next request. Model resolution supports configured provider/model boundaries, not unrestricted peer role creation.

live_collaboration.detail: Parent can queue, interrupt/restart, resume/wait/close live children, including managed subprocesses, but there is no traced peer room. First queued follow-up changes Running to Waiting; another while Waiting calls unguarded restart/launch and overwrites its handle, source-inferred overlapping runs for one child record.

concurrent_work.detail: Native readonly tool groups overlap and independent children/retained subprocesses can run concurrently; mutations remain governed by admission/group ordering. Repeated queued input has a separate per-child ownership concern.

steering_interrupt.detail: Operator steering/settings are consumed at request boundaries; Ctrl+C races a nonstreaming request. Child interrupt aborts current task and clears queued prompts, ordinary follow-ups should continue afterward; source concern in Waiting transition is retained.

turn_redefinition.detail: Compiled TurnHandlerOutcome and harness mode filters govern stop/continue/primary-agent handoff. Hooks can rewrite arguments and alter context and skills can change tools, but no hot programmable replacement of the full turn protocol was established.

compaction.detail: Manual/auto/recovery paths support provider-native or local summaries, reject noop/growing results, preserve opaque replay output, clear response chains and emit boundaries. Tests protect exact current-turn suffix and failure atomicity.

context_repair.detail: When dynamic persistence is enabled, compaction writes original rendered context plus a linked memory envelope for shell retrieval. It supports model recovery of details but lacks a traced native model-authorized restore/merge operation; history rendering and ten-file retention have limits.

original_audit.detail: Production canonical events have ordered/backpressured persistence and drain error reporting, more than optional trajectory logging. Default 10,000-event retention rewrites original completed-turn bytes into counts/kinds/selected facts; rendered compaction history also changes representation and timestamps. No original-everything guarantee.

audit_query.detail: Operator session-store exposes list/inspect/facts and audit pack creation/verification, with retained-turn reconstruction in the store. Verification proves current retained files match a pack, not complete original capture; model shell can inspect artifacts.

hot_change.detail: Model/effort applies after an in-flight request at the next request boundary, possibly before the current turn ends; accepted idle config reload preserves old state on parse errors. Model skill activation refreshes catalog but active skill content is cached. These differ from after-whole-turn/workflow activation.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Updater relaunch retains argv/cwd and replaces the process after CLI dispatch; current session is not injected unless original argv already supplies it. Desired background subprocess state can respawn but not retain process identity. Finalization can detach provider-backed memory work, so required refit quiescence/handoff is not established.

remote_services.detail: Consumes provider HTTP/websocket/compatibility requests and discovered MCP/web tooling; native codex-provider path delegates to a separate App Server runtime. This does not govern a shared compute/service fabric.

self_improvement.detail: Dynamic skills and a bounded verifier API support changing programs/instructions and reviewing changes. Default worktree reconciliation uses a heuristic verifier, not that API. No governed measured harness autoresearch or executable refit protocol was established.

complaints.detail: Operator /feedback opens a GitHub issue chooser. It neither exposes model rageshake nor captures context/agent state into a tracked external complaint DB or bead.

authority.detail: Admission revalidates hook-rewritten args, then checks concrete command/sandbox and configured safety/permission policies, agent mode and delegation hints. skip_confirmations changes interaction rather than all execution constraints.

evaluation.detail: Inspected source tests check failed-compaction history identity, exact suffix/boundary count, 3,253 canonical events/unique IDs, real PTY reaping and layered reload rollback. Synthetic tree tests do not prove live message isolation; no tests were executed.

time_order.detail: Serialized canonical event admission preserves caller order; prompt schedules distinguish cron, intervals and local one-shot times; request/wait cancellation uses Tokio deadlines. This is local ordering/deadlines, not a cross-service total causal clock.

evidence.claim: A bootstrap thread drives the Rust entrypoint; the runtime is not inferred from the npm distribution.
Main builds a multithreaded Tokio runtime with configured workers.
Provider codex selects a separate CodexSessionRuntime; other sessions select the native unified runtime.
Steering and pending model/effort settings are applied before the next request, after the previous in-flight request finished, potentially within the same turn.
Each request captures current model/capability/tool state and constructs and validates the provider request.
Nonstreaming generation races a Ctrl+C notification and keepalive timer, so cancellation can drop a waiting provider future.
Concrete OpenAI generation builds a Responses payload and submits authorized HTTP, with distinct streaming/websocket and compatibility paths.
Admission and pre-tool hooks precede safety/permission checks; rewritten arguments are revalidated rather than inheriting old validation.
Prepared calls dispatch to batch or individual execution and recover blocked/preflight responses on exits.
Admitted read-only parallel groups use FuturesUnordered; cancel notifiers race execution and results are recorded as each completes.
Success/failure/timeout/cancellation is paired with the call; model history is updated before UI rendering, then continuation or compiled primary-agent handoff is selected.
Public routing expressly excludes legacy unified action and read_file/list_files/write_file/edit_file names; internal registration does not establish model exposure.
Agent and code_search are exposed native operations; agent aliases are registered, and web_fetch defaults to prompted permission.
mcp and search_tools are exposed discovery/management operations; exec_command/write_stdin are model operations, while exec_pty_cmd is hidden.
Shell preparation validates concrete command policy and sandbox scope before execution; skipping confirmation does not remove these checks.
Command execution creates an owned pipe or PTY session, captures output, and returns stable session metadata with bounded yielding/background retention.
write_stdin actually dispatches only write, poll or wait; broader terminate/inspect/close language elsewhere does not expand this dispatcher.
Public execution schemas expose cmd/background/tty/workdir/output limits and session wait deadlines; a wait timeout returns an ongoing handle instead of killing it.
Execution manager closes all owned sessions for full termination, while active-session cancellation excludes retained background sessions.
The force-termination test checks a bounded return and a real observed exit status, then verifies close completes.
Native memory offers view/create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename under /memories; writable preferences/repository facts/notes are persistent files, not a general DB.
cron creates, lists and deletes session prompt tasks from exactly one cron/fixed-interval/local-time schedule.
The cron model description explicitly scopes scheduled prompts to the current VTCode process lifetime.
The exposed agent dispatcher requires an active controller and calls spawn, managed subprocess, send_input, resume, wait and close.
First noninterrupt input marks Running/Queued as Waiting and queues work; interrupt aborts the handle and replaces queued prompts, while other states launch a restart.
Delegation checks operator turn hints/selected agent; write-capable automatic delegation is restricted, with explicit agent choice providing another admission path.
launch_child spawns a fresh task and overwrites the stored handle; child_loop dequeues work by child ID. It does not guard against another live task for that ID.
restart_child fills an empty queue from last prompt and unconditionally calls launch_child, without cancelling or checking an existing handle.
Each child run dequeues a prompt and later mutates shared status, summary and stored context; two concurrent loops for one record can race those updates.
Background restoration reads desired-enabled records and respawns helpers whose exec-session identity is no longer live; this is restoration of intent, not old OS process identity.
A programmable verifier API spawns a bounded read-only review child and parses explicit decisions/issue lines with a keyword fallback; no verifier rejects.
Automatic worktree reconciliation instead uses HeuristicDiffVerifier inside spawn_blocking, not the asynchronous LLM-verifier API.
Manual compaction supports provider standalone/native-inline/local strategies, operates on cloned input and rejects unchanged/nonshrinking results.
Compaction runs a precompact hook, preserves opaque provider replay output, writes a memory/history envelope first, replaces history and resets response-chain/token state.
Original-context text artifacts are written only when dynamic context and persist_history are enabled; the memory envelope links the artifact for later retrieval.
History files default to a ten-file retention cap; they are configurable persisted context, not an unlimited archive.
History conversion renders text, reasoning and tool calls into strings and gives messages a shared conversion timestamp; it is not original typed/wire payload preservation.
Production constructs an authoritative canonical session sink before the session, independently of optional legacy exports.
Canonical event handoff serializes caller order and can backpressure; optional WebMCP consumer failures do not disable canonical persistence.
Finalization drains canonical persistence and reports failures, while legacy export losses are only diagnostics.
The canonical sink opens the event store with DEFAULT_MAX_EVENTS and drains accepted records on a blocking worker through a bounded queue.
Canonical event retention defaults to 10,000 events, retaining a summary before oldest completed turns are evicted.
Retention replaces the event file with remaining bytes after writing a summary; original evicted event bytes are removed.
The default eviction artifact holds counts, event kinds and selected grounded facts, rather than complete evicted events.
Operator session-store can migrate/GC/list/inspect/query facts and create or verify an audit pack against retained files.
Native list_skills/load_skill_resource/load_skill tools are wired to the session registry, snapshot notification and optional child-agent fork executor.
Traditional skill activation registers a new tool and refreshes current catalog; active skills return AlreadyActive and do not reread their content.
Config reload test observes valid creation/deletion and preserves the last valid draft after malformed input.
Idle session reload publishes accepted config and retains old configuration on rejected reloads.
Update relaunch preserves original argv/cwd and flushes output, then Unix exec replaces the process; it does not create an outpost or inject current session state.
Normal finalization may detach a provider-backed persistent-memory task after a five-second kickoff wait; this does not establish no-provider-request quiescence.
Exit/cancel/error performs best-effort owned-exec cleanup, while other transition reasons do not establish global quiescence.
Operator feedback opens an ordinary GitHub new-issue URL through a guarded browser action, without agent-state complaint capture.
Code-search dispatch is native. Hidden code execution spawns a configured external interpreter and supplies an MCP/builtin SDK, rather than a resident kernel.
Code execution generates SDK plus a unique temporary program; the IPC directory is workspace-wide.
Code execution runs a fresh process, parses stdout JSON and removes program/IPC files, with a bounded wait for the IPC handler.
Harness kernel functions filter compiled tool catalogs/mode/action exposure; they are not a programmable computation kernel or a replaceable turn program.
A failing mock compactor must preserve exact preexisting history.
Recovery-compaction test checks an identical current-turn suffix, shrinking prefix, cleared response ID and exactly one boundary event.
Canonical drain test writes 3,253 events then checks exact line count and unique event IDs.
Synthetic child-tree records verify close cascades and reopen queues descendants; this does not prove live concurrent execution isolation.
Model-override test observes effective child model selection; model choice is distinct from a shared colleague room.
search_tools explicitly expands deferred tools for the next request segment rather than instantly mutating an in-flight request.
apply_patch is a prompted native operation and dynamic skill catalog names are explicitly identified.
Permission flow applies approvals/denials/interrupts with runtime agent permissions, policy and skip_confirmations; hook phases are not rerun.
start_planning and task_tracker are registered native tools with workflow-dependent schemas and checklist aliases.
Planning tracker actions create/update/list/add carry hierarchical indexes, file/outcome and verification-command metadata.
web_search is a prompted public query tool; defuddle_fetch is registered but explicitly model-hidden.
Native MCP action dispatch actually invokes search/details/list/connect/disconnect handlers.

tests.focus: Force termination must reap a real PTY child, not merely return success.
tests.oracle: Creates /bin/sh sleep child, enforces 8-second kill budget, then observes an exit status within two seconds and bounded close; read only, not executed.

tests.focus: Provider compaction failure and recovery prefix/suffix boundaries.
tests.oracle: Mock failure preserves exact original vector; successful recovery preserves exact current-turn suffix, shrinks, clears response ID and emits one correct boundary. Mocks do not establish provider opaque replay conformance.

tests.focus: Canonical bounded-handoff drain and event identity.
tests.oracle: After 3,253 accepted events, close must yield exactly 3,253 lines with distinct IDs; checks accepted-event persistence, not raw-provider capture or retention completeness.

tests.focus: Reload malformed or newly created/deleted config layer.
tests.oracle: Observe provider changes for valid layer, exact prior provider after malformed layer, defaults after deletion. This is config activation, not executable refit.

tests.focus: Close/resume descendant cascade and model override.
tests.oracle: Synthetic parent/child/grandchild records become closed then queued; separate override test observes effective model. Neither drives two noninterrupt messages to an actually busy child, the discriminating race oracle still missing.

strengths: Production canonical sink is opened before session, isolates optional exporters, backpressures and reports drain errors.
Compaction failure atomicity, current-turn suffix preservation and conditional history artifacts explicitly address recoverability.
Execution handle lifecycle has a strong bounded PTY reap assertion; readonly group parallelism and child restoration are concrete mechanisms.
Dynamic traditional skills refresh session tools and deferred tools activate at a named request segment.
limits: Optional Codex App Server internals, provider variants, full web implementations, OS sandbox/process-tree semantics and complete checkpoint navigation are outside this trace. No paid/network/refit/concurrent-child experiments were run. Canonical events are retained rather than unlimited originals, and the inferred Waiting/restart overlap requires an independent controlled oracle.
arconaut_questions: Hold one child provider response, send two noninterrupt follow-ups, and assert one active runner and one owned JoinHandle for its ID; can Waiting ever trigger a second live run?
What records must be retained before canonical event caps or compaction to permit original-byte replay, causal study and model repair?
Should a next-request model/catalog activation wait for the entire current turn or affected workflow by default, with explicit interruption for immediate activation?
Before update/refit, can an oracle prove zero owned live commands and provider requests, including detached persistent-memory finalization, and preserve context through an outpost?
How can externally shared kernels/DBs be consumed through these action handles without moving their lifecycle governance into the harness?
